featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Some restaurants become popular, while others become part of a city’s collective memory. Paul’s Chinese in Dadar firmly belongs to the latter category. For decades, it has been serving generations of Mumbaikars, earning a reputation that stretches from local food lovers to cricketing legend Sachin Tendulkar himself. Yet despite its fame, Paul’s has retained the authenticity and soul that made it a neighbourhood favourite in the first place.
The food here is everything Mumbai-style Chinese should be bold, comforting, flavourful, and immensely satisfying. Every dish arrives packed with the unmistakable aromas and flavours that have made Paul’s an institution.
The legendary Chicken Chopper Rice is an absolute masterpiece and a must-order. Hearty, indulgent, and loaded with flavour, it perfectly captures the restaurant’s signature style. Equally impressive is the Triple Rice, a beloved classic that delivers the perfect balance of rice, noodles, gravy, and textures in every bite. The Hakka Noodles are expertly prepared, with just the right amount of wok hei and seasoning that keeps you reaching for more.
One of the highlights of the meal was undoubtedly the Paul’s Special Non-Veg Box, a generous feast that showcases the kitchen’s greatest hits in one satisfying package. The Veg Box is equally impressive and proves that vegetarian diners are in for just as memorable an experience.
The starters deserve special applause. Whether it’s the succulent chicken preparations, fresh seafood delicacies, or the surprisingly delicious vegetarian offerings, every dish demonstrates why Paul’s continues to command such a loyal following. The seafood is particularly noteworthy… fresh, perfectly cooked, and packed with flavour without being overwhelmed by sauces.
Beyond the food, the service reflects the warmth of a family-run legacy. The staff are courteous, attentive, and efficient, handling the bustling crowds with ease while ensuring guests feel welcome and comfortable. There is a sense of familiarity and genuine hospitality that is increasingly rare in today’s dining scene.
What makes Paul’s truly special is the legacy it carries. This is not just a restaurant; it is a Mumbai institution. Countless college students, office-goers, families, late-night food seekers, and loyal regulars have grown up eating here. The fact that it remains a favourite across generations is perhaps the greatest testament to its quality and consistency.
In a city overflowing with new restaurants and fleeting food trends, Paul’s Chinese continues to stand tall because it understands something timeless: great food, generous portions, warm service, and consistency never go out of style.
Whether you’re a first-time visitor or a lifelong regular, a meal at Paul’s feels like reconnecting with an old friend. A true Dadar legend and one of Mumbai’s most iconic Chinese dining destinations.

featured_reviews.review_text: Today, I visited Paul’s Chinese after watching a YouTube video that recommended their chicken triple Schezwan fried rice. featured_reviews.name: Sarbjeet Singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Paul Chinese in Matunga West is a go-to spot for classic Indo-Chinese food that’s flavorful, affordable, and filling. The place has a simple, no-frills setup focused entirely on serving fast, tasty meals.

I tried the Chicken Manchurian (Dry), Veg Fried Rice, and Schezwan Noodles. The Chicken Manchurian was the standout—perfectly cooked with a bold, tangy-spicy sauce. The Veg Fried Rice was light and well-balanced, while the Schezwan Noodles, though spicy, could’ve used a bit more flavor depth.

Service is quick and efficient, even when it’s busy. Portion sizes are generous and the pricing is student-friendly. If you're in Matunga West and craving Indo-Chinese, this place won’t disappoint.

Highlights:

Tasty, classic Indo-Chinese dishes

Fast service

Great portion size and value for money

Room for Improvement:

Schezwan dishes could use more flavor complexity

Ambience is basic—more focused on function than feel

Overall, a reliable and satisfying option for quick Chinese meals in the area.

featured_reviews.name: viraj pai
featured_reviews.review_text:
Paul Chinese is a fairly ordinary Chinese eatery with a basic setup. The restaurant has two floors—while the upper floor is air-conditioned, it has a very low ceiling which requires you to bend while walking. The ground floor, on the other hand, is non-AC and offers minimal comfort.
We ordered Chicken Lollipop with gravy, Triple Schezwan Fried Rice, and Chopper Rice for three people. The Chicken Lollipop was decent but nothing exceptional. The Triple Schezwan Fried Rice came with a red-colored gravy that looked artificial and lacked any real flavor. The dish had a strong eggy smell, which was quite off-putting. The Chopper Rice was bland, with barely any vegetables, and felt underwhelming in both taste and presentation.

We decided to try this place after watching a positive review on YouTube. However, our experience was disappointing and makes us question the authenticity of such glowing reviews, which may very well be paid promotions. Dining here felt like a gamble that, unfortunately, didn’t pay off—leaving us with an unpleasant aftertaste, both literally and figuratively.
